candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — identify medication contraindications, question potentially unsafe prescriptions, and administer IV medications safely
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — IV labetalol contraindication in bronchial asthma
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize bronchial asthma as a contraindication to IV labetalol and connect that safety concern to the drug's nonselective beta-adrenergic blocking activity.

options.A: Clarify the order because IV labetalol has nonselective beta-blocking activity and bronchial asthma is a labeled contraindication.
options.B: Administer the medication because labetalol blocks only alpha1 receptors and has no beta2 effect in the airways.
options.C: Administer the medication because severe hypertension removes the asthma contraindication.
options.D: Give the dose and assess for bronchospasm only after administration because asthma is not listed as a contraindication.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current FDA/DailyMed labeling describes labetalol as having selective alpha1-adrenergic blocking and nonselective beta-adrenergic blocking actions and lists bronchial asthma as a contraindication to IV labetalol. Because beta2 blockade can worsen bronchospasm, the nurse should clarify the order before giving the medication. B misstates labetalol's receptor profile. C and D incorrectly disregard a labeled contraindication.
candidate.source_claim_supported: IV labetalol combines alpha1 and nonselective beta blockade and is contraindicated in bronchial asthma; a nurse should clarify an order before administration when a labeled contraindication is present.
candidate.source_locator: Description/Clinical Pharmacology — selective alpha1-adrenergic and nonselective beta-adrenergic receptor blocking actions; Contraindications — bronchial asthma, overt cardiac failure, greater-than-first-degree heart block, cardiogenic shock, severe bradycardia, and other conditions associated with severe/prolonged hypotension
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration
candidate.stem: A client with severe hypertension and active bronchial asthma has a new order for IV labetalol. Which action should the nurse take before administration?
